newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds seen maintaining upward momentum.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds seen maintaining upward momentum.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which tracked higher with their European neighbours on Tuesday, are expected to keep climbing despite the growing feeling the market is too expensive, traders said.
"The undertone is still positive for Belgium. Everybody thinks we are too expensive but as long as end investors are still there we will keep going," one trader said.

Traders said the market came off earlier highs in quiet afternoon trading as players took profits when the benchmark German Bund broke through 103. But they noted that the spread over Bunds remained virtually unchanged.
"Investors are not touching the two to five years, there is no yield left there. The long end, 10 to 20 years, is the only area where there is still some yield left," the trader said.
The benchmark March 2007 OLO ended the day yielding 5.64 percent against Monday's closing 5.68 percent. The spread over Bunds was six basis points, one bp less than Monday.
The March futures contract was 23 basis points higher at 122.88.
"Overall it was very quiet out there today. There was a bit more activity than yesterday but nothing worth mentioning," one trader said.
Traders said the main focus of what activity there was on Tuesday was in long maturity paper -- 10 years and over -- with the short end neglected.
"The very long end was very well bid," one trader said. "There are people playing arbitrage there against Germany and France."
"The two to five years underperformed the market, and the five to 10 years flattened a bit," he added.
